The test image shows soybean stems at soil level with severe dark brown to black necrosis/discoloration on the lower stems near the soil line. Some stems are completely dead/dried. Key features: dark stem lesions near soil, plant death, one green stem visible on left.

Top candidates: Phytophthora (dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration from soil upward), Rhizoctonia (stem lesion near soil), Charcoal_Rot (gray stems with tiny black specks).
Now let me check one more reference to confirm:

**Analysis summary:**

**Test image key features:**
- Severely dead/dying plants at soil level
- Very dark brown to near-black stem discoloration at and above the soil line
- Multiple plants affected in the field
- Late season (dry pods visible in background on other plants)
- One healthy green stem for contrast

**Reference comparison:**
- **Phytophthora**: Best match — reference shows similar field death pattern with plants completely wilted/dead, dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration rising from soil line upward. The top-left quadrant mirrors the test scene closely
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows reddish-brown lesions on hypocotyl — more reddish than the very dark brown/black in the test image
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Shows pale/gray bleached stems with dark internal tissue — doesn't match the external dark coloring
- **Anthracnose**: Primarily pod/leaf symptoms — doesn't match

The dark chocolate-brown discoloration extending from the soil line upward with complete plant death is the hallmark of Phytophthora root rot.
